# Part III review {#sec-review-3 .unnumbered}

These exercises mix ideas from Parts I to III. They don't say which chapter they come from, so part of each exercise is deciding which tools to use. Solutions, with the chapters each exercise draws on, are in [Solutions: Part III](../appendices/solutions-3.qmd#sec-solutions-review-3).

1. []{#exercise-review-3-1}Are the vectors $(2, 1, 0)\T$, $(1, 2, 1)\T$ and $(1, -1, -1)\T$ linearly independent? If not, write one of them as a combination of the others, and describe their span geometrically. What is the determinant of the matrix with these columns?

   [Solution to exercise 1](../appendices/solutions-3.qmd#solution-review-3-1){.sol-link}

2. []{#exercise-review-3-2}Find the coordinates of $\vect{v} = (5, 1)\T$ in the basis $\vect{b}_1 = (1, 1)\T$, $\vect{b}_2 = (1, -1)\T$. Then find the matrix, in this basis, of the reflection $\M{S} = \mat{0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0}$, and explain why it comes out so simple.

   [Solution to exercise 2](../appendices/solutions-3.qmd#solution-review-3-2){.sol-link}

3. []{#exercise-review-3-3}For
   $$\M{A} = \mat{1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 4 & 3},$$
   find the rank, and a basis for each of the four fundamental subspaces. Check that the dimensions agree with rank–nullity. Is $\M{A}\vect{x} = \vect{b}$ solvable for every $\vect{b}$ in $\R^2$? When it is solvable, is the solution unique?

   [Solution to exercise 3](../appendices/solutions-3.qmd#solution-review-3-3){.sol-link}

4. []{#exercise-review-3-4}Fit a straight line $y = c_0 + c_1 x$ by least squares to the points $(0, 1)$, $(1, 3)$, $(2, 4)$ and $(3, 4)$. Find the residuals, and check that they are orthogonal to both columns of the design matrix.

   [Solution to exercise 4](../appendices/solutions-3.qmd#solution-review-3-4){.sol-link}

5. []{#exercise-review-3-5}Find the orthogonal projection of $\vect{b} = (1, 2, 0)\T$ onto the plane spanned by $(1, 0, 1)\T$ and $(0, 1, 1)\T$, and the distance from $\vect{b}$ to the plane.

   [Solution to exercise 5](../appendices/solutions-3.qmd#solution-review-3-5){.sol-link}

6. []{#exercise-review-3-6}Let $\M{A} = \mat{4 & 1 \\ 2 & 3}$ and $\M{P} = \mat{1 & 1 \\ 1 & -2}$. Find $\M{P}^{-1}\M{A}\M{P}$. What does the answer tell you about how $\M{A}$ acts on the lines through $(1, 1)$ and $(1, -2)$?

   [Solution to exercise 6](../appendices/solutions-3.qmd#solution-review-3-6){.sol-link}

7. []{#exercise-review-3-7}A $5 \times 7$ matrix $\M{A}$ has rank 4.

   a. What are the dimensions of its null space, column space, row space and left null space?
   b. Is $\M{A}\vect{x} = \vect{b}$ solvable for every $\vect{b}$ in $\R^5$?
   c. When it is solvable, how many free parameters does the general solution have?
   d. Can the columns of $\M{A}$ be linearly independent?

   [Solution to exercise 7](../appendices/solutions-3.qmd#solution-review-3-7){.sol-link}

8. []{#exercise-review-3-8}**Code.** Write a Gram–Schmidt function that takes a matrix and returns a matrix $\M{Q}$ with orthonormal columns spanning the same space. Apply it to the columns $(1, 1, 0)\T$, $(1, 0, 1)\T$, $(0, 1, 1)\T$, check that $\M{Q}\T\M{Q} = \M{I}$, and compare $\M{Q}$ with the built-in QR factorisation.
